title: test(core): derive the `page` residual pin’s type face instead of annotating it (objectui#9978)
body:
Fixes #9978

Clause-②: no — nothing published moves. The only source file is a `*.test.ts` under `packages/core/src/**/__tests__/`, which `packages/core/tsconfig.json` excludes from the emit program, and `packages/core`'s `files` is `["dist","README.md","CHANGELOG.md","LICENSE"]`. No accept set is relaxed and no key on a published payload moves. (The card's claim comment carries `Seat:` / `Branch:` / `Thread-read:` and no `Clause-②:` line, so this one is written rather than copied.)

## Step zero — the diagnostic reproduced in a checkout before a line was changed

The card relays the gate's reading and states it was never reproduced by the filing seat. It is now.

`@objectstack/spec` built from `objectstack-ai/objectstack@6819dcbd610397ded7a1533dbedf8a481d20fbdf` (today's objectstack `main`, newer than the card's `87f776bd7210`), packed by `npm pack` as 2,039 files / 28,974,627 B, injected into pnpm's virtual store by objectui#9877's own `scripts/spec-main-shape-gate.mjs inject` run from that branch's copy — the script is **not** part of this diff. Every leg below is `TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm exec turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/core --concurrency=2`, serialized behind the shared verify lock.

The instrument was read before it was used, and the reading discriminates:

| probe, from the INJECTED artifact | subject `page` | control `grid` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `ListViewSchema.shape.type.removeDefault().options` | absent | present |
| `const x: ViewType = LITERAL` under `tsc` | `TS2322` | compiles |

⇒ not a probe where subject and control come back the same way. The injected copy carries the marker `{"upstream":"objectstack-ai/objectstack","sha":"6819dcbd…","version":"17.4.0"}`; after the verification the published `17.4.0` was restored and its vocabulary re-read (ten members, `page` back).

| leg | spec resolved | source | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| subject | built from objectstack `6819dcbd` | before this change | exit 2 — `src/utils/__tests__/normalize-list-view.pageResidual-8429.test.ts(146,13): error TS2322: Type '"page"' is not assignable to type 'ViewType'.` |
| subject | built from objectstack `6819dcbd` | **after** | that diagnostic is **gone** |
| control | published `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` | **after** | exit 0 |

⚠️ The package still exits 2 on the injected leg, on the OTHER diagnostic — `object-validation-engine.test.ts(162,9)`, which is objectui#9979 and is untouched here. Stated so nobody reads this PR's remaining red as unfinished work on this card.

## The judgement the card asked for first: (A) — the spelling is the fixture's SUBJECT

Not a preference; the file says so three times, quoted rather than paraphrased. The test the line sits in is named

> `it('keeps `page` on BOTH published `@object-ui/types` faces', () => {`

the comment directly above the line is

> `// The type face. This line is a COMPILE-time assertion as much as a`
> `// runtime one: narrowing `ViewType` makes the annotation itself an error.`

and the file header names the very failure as a designed outcome:

> `*   · narrow `ViewType` ⇒ the published faces stop accepting `page` ⇒ RED.`

⇒ ⛔ (B) is ruled out: it is not a convenient literal in a test about something else. Deleting the spelling, or swapping it for a member that still exists, would delete the pin.

## The repair: change what the value is checked against, not the value

An annotation judges the literal against whichever `ViewType` is RESOLVED, which is exact in the one direction nobody wants here: it turned an UPSTREAM retirement into the pin failing to **compile**, on the single leg where that retirement is the news. That is objectui#9880's and objectui#9943's class, and this is their move applied to a fixture.

`@object-ui/types` derives its two published faces from two DIFFERENT exports of the spec —

```ts
export type ViewType = NonNullable<SpecListView['type']> | 'list' | 'detail';                 // views.ts
export const ViewTypeSchema = z.enum([...SpecListViewTypeEnum.options, 'list', 'detail']);    // zod/views.zod.ts
```

— and the zod-mirror ledger registers `views.zod.ts#ViewTypeSchema` as *"a bare vocabulary with no `.shape`; it is checked where a mirrored KEY declares it"*, i.e. nothing else compares the pair. So the claim the test is NAMED for, `page` on BOTH faces, is now checked as the two faces **agreeing** about it:

```ts
type ValueFaceViewType = (typeof ViewTypeSchema.options)[number];
type AssertNever<T extends never> = T;
type PageFaceSkew<TypeFace extends string, ValueFace extends string> =
  | Exclude<Extract<ValueFace, 'page'>, TypeFace>
  | Exclude<Extract<TypeFace, 'page'>, ValueFace>;

export type _LivePageFaceSkew = AssertNever<PageFaceSkew<ViewType, ValueFaceViewType>>;
```

`never` while both faces carry the kind, `never` while both drop it together, a live union — `TS2344` — the moment either narrows alone. `Extract` is load-bearing exactly as it is in objectui#9880: a kind the spec has RETIRED drops out of the type instead of becoming an error.

⛔ Nothing the pin was for is deleted. `page`'s bare presence is still asserted, LITERALLY and at RUNTIME, against the spec this repository actually resolves — the sized ten- and twelve-member vocabularies, `ViewTypeSchema.safeParse('page')`, the single-member residual set, the twelve-row census and the misrouted-kinds property. Seventeen occurrences of the spelling remain in the file. ⚠️ What no compile-time spelling can state on both legs is `page`'s bare membership in the live union: that sentence is FALSE once the spec retires the kind, and the file now says so where the annotation used to be.

## The new assert fires, and the controls are not decoration

Any one run installs exactly one spec, so the firing half is lifted over SIMULATED vocabularies — same operator, same composition, both legs reachable from one compile. Two skew directions carry `@ts-expect-error`, and control C is the card's own diagnostic reproduced inside ordinary CI on the published leg, where the live union cannot produce it.

Ablation, on the PUBLISHED leg, from the committed state: neutralising `PageFaceSkew` so it can only answer `never` makes `tsc -p packages/core/tsconfig.test.json` print

```
…normalize-list-view.pageResidual-8429.test.ts(141,1): error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.
…normalize-list-view.pageResidual-8429.test.ts(145,1): error TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive.
```

⇒ both controls were suppressing a real error, and the operator is what produces it. Mutation proven on disk by anchor grep and blob hash `d86cab7e…` → `a9ac7ed2…`; restored to `d86cab7e…` by hash equality with an empty `git diff HEAD`, `trap` on EXIT/INT/TERM with absolute paths.

Ablation, on the INJECTED leg: reverting this file to its base blob `69bff4dd…` brings the card's diagnostic back — `…pageResidual-8429.test.ts(146,13): error TS2322: Type '"page"' is not assignable to type 'ViewType'.` — and restoring to `d86cab7e…` removes it again. Same proof discipline.

## Tests

| command | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/core` (published spec, after) | exit 0 |
| `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/core` (injected `6819dcbd`, after) | this file's `TS2322` gone; exit 2 remains on objectui#9979's line only |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/normalize-list-view.pageResidual-8429.test.ts` (repo root) | 1 file / 9 tests passed |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/utils/` (repo root) | 79 files / 1582 tests passed |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — 1 source file, 1 changeset, empty frontmatter |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` (final 2 paths) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:spec-symbols · check:changeset-claims · check:pending-changeset-literals · check:vi-mock-specifiers · check:vi-mock-inherit · check:vi-mock-override-shape · check:comment-mask-corpus · check:test-path-roots · check:new-line-citations · check:control-bytes` | exit 0, each |

`node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the final file list, verdict verbatim:

```
✅ NOT GOVERNED — 2 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.
   An ordinary pull request: the normal review and merge-queue route applies.
```

⚠️ `pnpm check:spec-symbols` is RED under the injected spec (six hand-written spec-named symbols across four packages, none in this diff) and green on the published one. Recorded so the injected leg's output is not read as a regression here.

### Lint, narrowed — population, count, invariance

- **Population.** The lint script is a plain `eslint .` per package via `turbo run lint`; ⛔ no `--no-inline-config`.
- **Count**, from eslint's own `--format json`: **1** file linted (the one changed `.ts`), **0** errors, **0** warnings. The changeset is `.md` and no config object matches it.
- **Invariance.** `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, so type-aware linting is not enabled and a change confined to one file cannot move the verdict on any file it did not touch. ⇒ the repo-wide run CI owns can differ from this one only on files this branch did not change.

Run on final head `ecec65378`.

## Acceptance notes — out of scope, noted, not fixed here

- **`object-validation-engine.test.ts(162,9)`** is the gate's other diagnostic and is already carried by **objectui#9979** (`pm:dispatched`). Not folded in: different member, different union, no relation to `ViewType`.
- Noted, not filed: the file's runtime half now carries the whole "narrow `ViewType` ⇒ RED" leg, so a future spec bump that retires the kind in a PUBLISHED release will redden this fixture in seven places at once rather than one. That is the intended loudness, and the carrier that would act on it is the pin-bump PR objectui#8429 is waiting for. Successor: the objectui#8429 disposition PR.
- Noted, not filed: `AGENTS.md:330` tells a green non-governed PR author to self-merge, and this dispatch forbids the ready flip. The conflict is filed as objectstack#19128; this PR acts on the stricter side and stops at draft.
